📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that AS SOMEONE RAISED on slasher horror movies, I was always going to gravitate towards LED face masks. But while their creepy Jason Voorhees-at-a-rave look is what initially grabbed my attention, the skincare benefits are what sold me on the products. LED face masks combine the firming power of anti-aging products, the depuffing of eye cream, the energizing boost of moisturizers, and the breakout-fighting strength of acne washes—making them one of the most versatile grooming tools out there.

According to recent reports, LED masks use specific wavelengths of light to penetrate the skin and trigger cellular changes, according to dermatologist Dr. Hannah Kopelman, MD. This can include stimulating collagen production to reduce fine lines and support firmer skin, as well as treating acne-causing bacteria and calming inflammation to promote a clearer complexion. Some devices offer all of these benefits, while others are laser-focused (get it?) on just one or two. The key is to know what each is capable of and what service you’re looking for.

According to recent reports, dermatologist Dr. Brian Toy, MD, warns that the market is flooded with LED face masks that vary greatly in quality and effectiveness, so it’s best to start your search as informed as possible. To temper the confusion, I went ahead and used myself, along with fellow Men’s Health writers and editors, as guinea pigs. This way, you’ll know what works and what is merely an overpriced Halloween mask.

According to recent reports, we gave Shark Beauty CryoGlow a 2025 Men’s Health Grooming Award barely a month after it was released; that’s how great this LED mask is. It offers four separate treatment options that cover anything you could possibly want out of an LED face mask. The Better Aging setting uses red and infrared light to reduce wrinkles and firm skin, while Skin Clearing mode combines blue, red, and infrared light to fight blemishes and even tone.

Recent findings suggest that the Skin Sustain maintains glow with a quick mix of all three LED wavelengths, and Under-Eye Revive uses cryotherapy-inspired cooling to depuff and tighten the under-eye area. You can also use this under-eye cooling ability combined with the other treatments, which roll out in three increasing levels of chill. Each is between four and eight minutes, meaning you don’t need to dedicate much time to combat whatever glitch you’re after. Under-Eye Revive, you can do up to 15 minutes if you’d like, but you only need five to be effective.

Dr. Peterson Pierre, MD, FAAD, likes that this device uses red, blue, and infrared lights so that you can get a full smorgasbord of benefits, like combating acne, fighting signs of aging, reducing inflammation, and helping regulate oil production. He also digs the cooling feature and three levels of intensity. I’ve been using my CryoGlow for months, and have seen a noticeable change in the smoothness and clearness of my skin, as well as reduced redness, using The Better Aging and Skin Clearing settings. But where I saw the most immediate results was with eye puffiness.

If I’m ever running on limited sleep or recovering from a night out, I pop the mask on, and after a few minutes of Under-Eye Revive mode, I look like I’ve actually slept. The light from this device doesn’t feel glaring when you’re wearing it, so I was able to successfully walk around and multitask during my treatments.

Industry observers note that plus, as someone who is generally sensitive to light, it also feels a lot less intense than other options on this list, and never inspired headaches of any kind. Not to mention, it’s easy to adjust and fits my face perfectly. I only have a few nitpicks. Given the expansive options and customizability of this mask, there is a handheld controller attached to it to help you navigate. While this makes firing up the device super easy and you don’t need to rely on an app, the controller can be a bit awkward to deal with while you’re in treatment.

According to recent reports, you can’t put it in your pocket without accidentally changing the setting, so you have to hold it, which limits the multitasking you’re able to do. Also, the mask is bulkier than its main competition for best overall, the Dr. Dennis Gross Face Mask. But when you consider that the CryoGlow is also the cheapest full-face option on this list, it’s a fair trade-off.

Read More: Shark CryoGlow LED Face Mask Review.

Dr. Kopelman has been recommending this LED mask to patients for years. She likes that it is FDA-cleared and offers both red and blue light; however, what she likes most about it is that it consistently delivers results. In terms of effectiveness, it’s equal to the CryoGlow. The only reason it just missed out on the top spot is that it’s over $100 more expensive and offers fewer additional treatments, like under-eye cooling. Beyond that, I find it just as successful at battling blemishes and signs of aging as the Shark Beauty.

Plus, the treatments are shorter, and you only need to wear this for three minutes a day to see results. Unlike many other options, like the CurrentBody or FAQ 202, which are made of more flexible material you can mold to your face, this design is rigid. While that may seem like a drawback, I loved it. Of all the LED masks on this list, I found Dr. Dennis Gross to be the sturdiest, and it fit my face perfectly. It’s slim, without feeling flimsy, and doesn’t weigh down my face like other similarly sturdy masks that tend to be a bit heavier, such as the Theraface Mask.

Sources indicate that that being said, I possess an incredibly average build and face shape, so if you fall outside of those parameters, the singular and unadaptable design of this mask might not be as perfect a fit. Unlike the CryoGlow, it’s wireless when you’re using it and can be conveniently charged with any USB-C charger. This helps when traveling, though the solid design poses some challenges if you’re tight on storage space.

Read More: Best Anti-Aging Products.

Similar to the Dr. Dennis Gross mask, this device is crafted with a hard, contoured shell; however, it’s far less slim. But it trades off this added bulkiness with its vibrating ability, which soothes facial tension and boosts blood flow around the eyes, brows, and scalp. It offers red, blue, and infrared light therapy to target acne, improve skin tone, and increase collagen production.

Recent findings suggest that you can choose between three- or nine-minute treatment modes, though we found the longer sessions to be more effective. Sure, this mask can feel a bit heavy or bulky on the face, but the results are legit. In fact, some effects can be seen immediately, and they only increase from there. “After the very first time I used it, my skin felt softer, and my pores looked smaller,” says Senior Gear and Commerce Editor Ryan Brower.

“Over time, my skin tone looks more even, and my skin appears to be firmer, smoother, and less puffy.” He adds that the massaging, vibrating feature is relaxing, although it can feel ticklish or even chill-inducing at times. Since it sits close to your ears, it can also get a bit loud, especially when multitasking. Still, it’s really easy to switch between settings, turn on and off, and choose the massage style you want.

Sources indicate that if you’re solely looking to combat puffiness, dark circles, and wrinkles, Lumin is the way to go. Sure, it looks straight out of an abandoned Lone Ranger In Space reboot, but there is no device better at rejuvenating the skin around the eyes than this mask. One tester saw noticeable improvements after days of use with this device. “I naturally have darker circles, but after consistent daily use for about a week, I saw a noticeable difference in the brightness and overall alertness of my eye area,” she says. The mask stays in place well, and the soft silicone padding makes it comfortable throughout each session.

It has been revealed that its adjustable design also ensures it fits all face shapes and sizes with ease. The same tester also saw a brighter tone and smoother skin after a couple of weeks of daily use. “While I don’t personally have under-eye wrinkles, I can see how this would be especially helpful for someone who does or for anyone who spends a lot of time in the sun,” she says. Not to mention, the Luminator is quick and easy to use—just three minutes a day with an auto timer.

Read More: Best Eye Cream for Men.

Our testers found that this FAQ mask makes a strong impression right out of the box with its ultra-thin, flexible design, which feels more like a high-end sheet mask than a tech device. You’ll need to download the app to get the most out of this tool, however. There’s a single button on the mask, but without the app, we found that it was nearly impossible to remember its function or how to power it off.

Recent findings suggest that once the app is set up and the mask is synced, navigating the features becomes straightforward—just select your desired treatment and that’s it. Despite being covered in tiny LED lights, the mask feels surprisingly lightweight and comfortable. During the 15-minute session, testers reported no heat or noticeable sensation on the skin and even forgot it was on while doing other tasks, such as reading. The mask stays comfortably in place, even when looking down at a book or phone.

In a recent development, we also appreciated the included cleaning spray. For anyone with sensitive or breakout-prone skin, keeping the mask clean is essential, and the spray makes that simple. After each use, we cleaned and dried the mask before placing it in its pouch, which securely holds the device and makes storage hassle-free. One minor concern was the split at the bridge of the nose—designed for flexibility—which left one tester wondering if that area was receiving full treatment. Still, this didn’t deter them from continuing to use it.

Industry observers note that women’s Health fitness contributor Nicolette Accardi states that the Qure Pro LED Mask has taken her nightly skincare regimen to the next level. After a month of use, she saw a dramatic difference in her skin’s appearance. She used to struggle with oily skin and frequent breakouts, but since regularly using the pink LED light setting, she says it has significantly reduced her sebum production. “I'm also approaching 30 (yikes), so I've been using the red LED light setting as well to help combat fine lines and reverse skin aging,” Accardi says.

Recent findings suggest that each session runs for three minutes and automatically shuts off when it’s done, so you never have to worry about timing it yourself. It’s perfect for anyone who wants results without the hassle. It’s one of the easiest, most low-maintenance skincare tools out there at a relatively low cost. That’s not to say $380 is cheap, but when it comes to legit, effective LED masks, you won’t find many other options under $400. It’s really just this and the CryoGlow.

It has been revealed that if the more rigid masks, like CryoGlow, Qure, and Dr. Dennis Gross, are too bulky for you, but the FAQ is too small for your face, Currentbody will be your best option. This mask offers the most flexibility, with a silicone design that easily molds to the contours of any face, ensuring full coverage. This is as long as you tighten the straps. I’ve been lazy a few times with that, and it will start slipping off your face mid-treatment. In addition to the flexible fit, this mask feels super gentle on the face.

One of our testers used it only days after getting eye surgery with no issue. Didn’t bother her eyes one bit. That being stated, it takes up to six hours for a full charge, which can be a bit annoying. This is the longest charge time on this list by a few hours, to be clear. I’m the type of person who pushes off charging a device until I absolutely have to, so this long charge time usually results in me skipping a day of treatment. But if you’re a better planner (to be fair, it’s a low bar compared to me), it’ll be less of an issue.

In a recent development, depending on what skin challenges or concerns you’re looking to address with your LED face mask, you’ll want to focus on which treatments it offers. This is driven by the color of light the device uses, which dictates its benefits. Some on this list offer multiple services, while others zero in on one. These are the common options:.

In a recent development, while some are comfortable and allow for multitasking, there is no getting around the fact that you’re wearing a large light on your face. As a long-time migraine sufferer, having a light this close to my eyes for too long can be a trigger. But even if you’re perfectly fine with prolonged light exposure, you’ll want to know what the time commitment is before buying LED face masks, as they’re most effective when used regularly. Some are as long as 25 minutes, while others can be as short as three minutes. Keep in mind that not all are meant for everyday use; some (especially the ones with longer treatment lengths) may only need to be used a few times a week for max efficiency.

Industry observers note that when shopping for an LED face mask, choosing a device that’s FDA-cleared is essential, states Dr. Kopelman. This ensures the product meets fundamental safety standards for consumer use. To be clear, however, FDA-cleared is not the same as FDA-approved—the latter involves extensive clinical trials and rigorous testing. At the moment, no LED face masks on the market have achieved FDA approval.

In a recent development, for now, stick with FDA-cleared options, which means the device is proven to be as safe and effective as another legally marketed product. You might also see terms like FDA-registered or FDA-listed, but these simply indicate that the manufacturer has notified the FDA of the product's existence—there’s no review or evaluation involved. Because of that uncertainty, you won’t see any of those on this list.

In a recent development, there are a lot of LED face masks out there, and like any trendy tool, not all are created equal. So, before putting any to the test, I consulted with a panel of dermatologists on which devices were legit and which they recommend. They also advised me on what to look for in a quality LED face mask and the brands to focus on. Based on this intel, I, along with other Men’s Health writers and editors, put several masks to the test, evaluating each device’s effectiveness, ease of use, and how comfortable it was to wear.

According to recent reports, as many LED face masks do not offer immediate results, we used each one for at least one month to ensure enough time was given to gain any possible benefits. Following this extensive research and testing, I landed on these seven LED face masks as the best for men in 2026.

According to recent reports, the dermatologists I spoke to for this story were clear on this: you should be cleaning your device after every use. If you don’t, bacteria, oil, and product residue can build up on the surface and transfer back onto your skin, causing irritation or breakouts, which may ironically be what you were hoping to minimize by using an LED mask in the first place.

Industry observers note that dr. Kopelman notes that LED masks should always be used on freshly cleansed, dry skin to ensure the light penetrates as effectively as possible. After the session, apply your serums and moisturizers—doing it beforehand can block the light and reduce its benefits. A hydrating serum like hyaluronic acid or a peptide-rich cream works especially well to complement the collagen boost from the treatment, Dr. Kopelman says.

According to Dr. Toy, be sure to skip any products that might react to light. For example, because retinol and vitamin C serums are photosensitizing, they’re an absolute no-go before any LED treatment. Dr. Chacon adds that reflective products like heavy oils or sunscreens should also be avoided during use as they can scatter the light and disrupt the device’s effectiveness.

Scout Motors starts validation builds at $2B SC plant, deliveries in 2028

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1079 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Volkswagen’s revived Scout brand finally has vehicles coming off the line in South Carolina, but they’re validation units, not customer cars.
  • That’s two years later than the 2026 production start the tech giant was talking about before it even broke ground on its $2 billion factory.
  • According to Scout’s announcement dated November 12, construction at the Production Center north of Columbia is in its final phase and most of the manufacturing equipment is installed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Volkswagen’s revived Scout brand finally has vehicles coming off the line in South Carolina, but they’re validation units, not customer cars. Scout confirms the first deliveries of the Traveler SUV and Terra pickup won’t happen until 2028.

That’s two years later than the 2026 production start the tech giant was talking about before it even broke ground on its $2 billion factory.

According to Scout’s announcement dated November 12, construction at the Production Center north of Columbia is in its final phase and most of the manufacturing equipment is installed. The Body Shop, Paint Shop, and Assembly Shop are all being used for the first validation builds.

The Body Shop is the most automated part of the plant. Scout says more than 750 robots join roughly 160 parts into each body, laying down about 5,000 weld points per vehicle, with AI-supported weld monitoring and a metrology system checking the results. At full capacity, the shop is designed to handle about 40 vehicles per hour.

Bodies then go through an electrified paint shop before landing in final assembly, where they’re married to the chassis and get their wiring, glass, seats, and wheels.

CEO Scott Keogh is clearly happy to have something physical to point to, saying that “what we are building in Blythewood is no longer a promise on paper.”.

Scout also shared photos of a Terra pickup and a Traveler parked inside the plant. Its own fine print notes that they show “concept and validation vehicles” with optional features, so don’t read too much into what’s on display:.

Recent findings suggest that fair enough. But Scout is also careful about what this stage is. Teams are confirming the equipment is installed and works, and checking engineering, buildability, and parts maturity. Process validation and scaling up to production speed come later. Validation builds will continue “into 2027,” followed by pre-production builds, and then customer deliveries in 2028.

The company indicates the plant will create more than 4,000 jobs, and it’s spending another $300 million on an onsite supplier park expected to support about 1,000 supplier jobs.

Sources indicate that when Keogh laid out the plan in late 2023, Scout remarked it would start production in 2026 with deliveries shortly after. That was still the target when Scout broke ground in Blythewood in February 2024.

By the Traveler and Terra unveiling in October 2024, production had moved to 2027. Keogh then said in March that he expects the first customer to get a vehicle “sometime in 2028,” and that’s now the official line in Scout’s own press materials.

It might not even be the end of it. Industry forecaster AutoForecast Solutions has the Traveler starting production in September 2028 and the Terra in March 2030. Scout hasn’t confirmed those dates, but it hasn’t given more precise ones either.

The product itself has also changed under the hood. Scout launched as a pure EV brand, then added the “Harvester” range-extender option at the reveal. According to Keogh, Scout has more than 160,000 reservations, and 87% of them are for the gas-generator version. Those are $100 refundable reservations, not orders.

Der Spiegel reported earlier this year that integrating the range extender, which wasn’t part of the original plan, was among the technical problems pushing the timeline back.

In a recent development, for comparison, Tesla unveiled the Cybertruck in November 2019 and delivered the first ones four years later, a delay that was widely mocked. Scout is now on a similar four-year path from reveal to customer, and that’s for the SUV it’s launching first.

Recent findings suggest that A working body shop with 750 robots isn’t vaporware. Scout has a real factory, a real workforce, and two vehicles that people clearly want. 160,000 reservations is a massive number for a brand that hasn’t sold a single vehicle in 46 years.

But validation builds are an early step, not a finish line. Scout still has to go through pre-production, prove its processes, and ramp to rate, and every one of those stages is where new automakers usually lose time. Rivian and Lucid both learned that the hard way.

September 28? So we're 23 months away? I'm surprised the validation build yadda yadda stuff is supposed to take so long. It's not like VW doesn't know how to do this stuff, and that's a lot of money and equipment to sit mostly idle while 180,000 reservations holders are waiting for their cars. Maybe they're waiting for the market to change or are considering a whole other brand or product line?

And the market Scout was designed for in 2022 no longer exists. The EV tax credit is gone, and most of Scout’s own reservation holders picked the gas generator. In the US, the range-extender market is still early, unlike in China, where they are already popular.

But by 2028, Ford, Ram, and Jeep all strategy to have range-extended trucks and SUVs on sale. Scout’s main advantage was being early with a cool, rugged, American-built electric truck. That advantage shrinks every quarter.

In a recent development, we’re still rooting for these vehicles. The Traveler and Terra are among the best-looking designs in the segment. But a $100 reservation is easy to walk away from, and the question is how many of those 160,000 people are still waiting in 2028.

If you’re planning to charge a Scout or any other EV at home, pairing it with rooftop solar can cut your fuel costs to nearly zero. Latest Update: Waymo halts highway operation nationwide after CA DMV pause

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (888 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Waymo has pulled its vehicles from highways nationwide after the California Department of Motor Vehicles ordered the company to pause highway operation in the state, following a viral video showing a Waymo trying to pass a police blockade.
  • According to recent reports, waymo is Google’s robotaxi subsidiary, which has been operating autonomously on public roads in some form since 2017.
  • The vehicles can be hailed through Waymo’s app, and operate with no driver in the driver’s seat, 24/7 in the covered areas.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Waymo has pulled its vehicles from highways nationwide after the California Department of Motor Vehicles ordered the company to pause highway operation in the state, following a viral video showing a Waymo trying to pass a police blockade.

According to recent reports, waymo is Google’s robotaxi subsidiary, which has been operating autonomously on public roads in some form since 2017. It has now expanded to 15 areas, recently adding another 250 square miles just last month.

The vehicles can be hailed through Waymo’s app, and operate with no driver in the driver’s seat, 24/7 in the covered areas. Since it can operate at any time but only within geofenced areas, this counts as “level 4” autonomy, as compared to the level 2 autonomy available on most consumer vehicles.

It has been revealed that until recently, Waymo only operated on city streets. These are more complex than highways, but lower speed. Accidents are more common on city streets than on highways, but can be more spectacular on highways given the higher speeds involved.

Most driver assist systems have been rolled out gradually, starting with highways, due to this lower complexity. But Waymo started with city streets first, bucking that trend.

The tech giant started offering rides on highways late last year, but only in limited markets. It had been testing highway operation for several years prior, typically with a driver and with no public ridership.

Everything was going pretty well, with Waymo declaring its autonomous vehicles have stopped 841 injuries over the course of their 271 million miles of operation. And in terms of competition, Waymo is far ahead of Tesla’s Robotaxi effort.

Recent findings suggest that but then, the viral internet stepped in. Last week, a video surfaced showing a Waymo trying to pass two police cars who were trying to slow down traffic on I-280 in Northern California. This is one of the main routes through Silicon Valley, and the opening of highway operations drastically reduced ride times in the area.

The video reveals two police cars behind a construction vehicle, lights on and spread out across the freeway. Then it pans to show a Waymo vehicle moving swiftly in the far left lane. One of the officers accelerates and swerves in front of the Waymo vehicle, at which point the Waymo swerves and slows down. (One media citation states that the video seems to have been sped up by the original poster, but we’ve embedded the short local news report on it above).

In response to this, the California DMV contacted Waymo and ordered the firm to pause highway operations while it examines the incident. The order was made on November 11, but wasn’t reported until today.

In a recent development, the DMV cited multiple instances of Waymo vehicles incurring into construction zones, not simply the one viral clip above. It said that previous incidents had occurred and been noted, and corrective actions were implemented, but that the incidents keep happening.

According to recent reports, this is a very rare situation which Waymo handled poorly. Waymo will add this case to their their test suite. They'll probably ask the CHP for their in car videos of other cases and convert those to be additional test cases. Waymo has been very willing to admit when their vehicles make mistakes in rare situations and fix it so that it doesn't happen again.

Waymo's vehicles are compared against perfect driving and Waymo accepts that as an aspirational goal. I note Tesla lacks the confidence in their system to even apply for the California permit to begin autonomous testing.

DMV’s pause will remain until Waymo can demonstrate “effective corrective actions” have been taken.

While the DMV’s order only applies to California highways, Waymo also paused highway operations in other states. It remains operating on city streets in all coverage areas.

Revision: Waymo emailed us this statement after it saw this article.

“Safety is at the foundation of everything we do. Following recent freeway construction zone encounters on U.S. 101 in California that did not involve any injuries or collisions, the California DMV has implemented an operating restriction on freeway operations in the state. In alignment with our safety-first principles, we have also temporarily restricted freeway operations across our other operating markets to evaluate our performance. Our ride-hailing service continues to operate safely on surface streets, serving over half a million trips each week. We are working with the California DMV and other state officials diligently and responsibly to resume freeway operations.”.

All the comfort of regular cotton, but grown without harsh chemicals. It's eco-friendly and feels extra gentle on your skin.

Providing the right care to your tees will help keep them looking sharp and feeling comfy for eons. First up, read the damn label! Make sure you follow the washing instructions. Also, be sure to separate colors when you wash T-shirts (i.e. darks with darks and lights with lights).

Industry observers note that when you wash, make sure the water is cold because the temperature will help preserve colors and prevent shrinkage. Turning T-shirts inside out can also help protect the outer fabric from friction and fading. Use a gentle cycle and mild detergent to help maintain the shape and fabric, too.

Recent findings suggest that additionally, skip the dryer and air-dry if possible because high heat can cause shrinkage (use low-heat settings if you must air-dry). We also recommend folding instead of hanging T-shirts because the latter will stretch out the neck of the tees and cause them to lose their shape.

Sources indicate that these are two indicators of whether your T-shirt can or should be tucked in or left untucked. With a curved hem, then the tee is best left untucked; it'll probably look better that way. A straight hem can do both, depending on the length. That is to say, a longer length is thus best left tucked in, unless you've got the height or the style magic to offset any disproportion.

Walking, Yoga, or Zumba? Which Exercises Help Relieve Menopause Mood Symptoms

📅 17 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (746 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Physical activity may help support mood and improve quality of life during the menopause transition, according to a study published on October 13 in Menopause, the journal of the Menopause Society.
  • This review of 12 clinical trials involving over 1,000 people ages 40 to 65 found that both aerobic and mind-body exercises may be associated with reduced depressive symptoms and improved well-being.
  • In a recent development, it is common for individuals to experience psychological symptoms during menopause, including depression, anxiety, low mood, stress, and difficulty with thinking and memory.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Physical activity may help support mood and improve quality of life during the menopause transition, according to a study published on October 13 in Menopause, the journal of the Menopause Society.

This review of 12 clinical trials involving over 1,000 people ages 40 to 65 found that both aerobic and mind-body exercises may be associated with reduced depressive symptoms and improved well-being.

In a recent development, it is common for individuals to experience psychological symptoms during menopause, including depression, anxiety, low mood, stress, and difficulty with thinking and memory. These symptoms can have a significant effect on quality of life, with an estimated 1 in 10 women leaving work due to menopause symptoms.

This study found that regular physical activity may help improve certain psychological symptoms and overall quality of life during menopause.

The types of physical activity in the review were broken into two categories: aerobic-based exercise (ABIs) and mind-body activities (MBAs).

The researchers found that ABIs indicated the strongest effects on reducing depressive symptoms and improving overall quality of life. This may be particularly relevant during perimenopause when women may be more vulnerable to mood instability due to estrogen fluctuations.

Sherry Ross, MD, board certified OB/GYN and Women’s Health Expert at Providence Saint John’s Health Center in Santa Monica, CA, who wasn’t involved in the study, pointed out that there are various ways that ABIs can have positive effects.

Ross explained that aerobic exercise may help improve menopausal symptoms through several mechanisms, including the release of endorphins, reduced inflammation, improved cholesterol levels, and better regulation of body temperature and sleep cycles.

According to recent reports, MBAs were shown to have a greater effect on improving psychological quality of life. These exercises involve mindfulness, body awareness, and breathwork. They may help improve emotional regulation.

ABIs tended to require fewer sessions. This may mean these types of exercises are easier to fit in, especially if you are facing time or energy constraints. For example, in one trial, participants were instructed to walk for 30 minutes, three times per week. In another trial, participants attended three hour-long Zumba classes per week.

In contrast, one trial using MBAs instructed participants to attend two 75-minute yoga classes each week, and another had participants attend daily one-hour yoga classes.

Stephanie Faubion, MD, Director for the Mayo Clinic Center for Women’s Health and Medical Director for The Menopause Society, who wasn’t involved in the study, told Healthline that these findings are encouraging.

Industry observers note that however, she also cautioned that this was a relatively small body of evidence. “While physical activity is an notable component of a healthy lifestyle during midlife, I would be cautious about interpreting these findings to mean that exercise is a treatment for depression related specifically to menopause,” she stated.

Research has shown that physical activity can positively affect mental health. Studies have also found that regular exercise can help improve symptoms of depression and anxiety.

Faubion told Healthline that, broadly speaking, regular physical activity may support mood through multiple pathways, including better sleep, improved physical function, and overall well-being.

However, she also noted that this study cannot tell us precisely why the improvements occurred or whether aerobic exercise is superior to other forms of activity.

Faubion said that recommending physical activity during and after menopause extends well beyond mood.

“Physical activity is key for cardiovascular and metabolic health, maintaining muscle mass and physical function, and supporting bone health,” she remarked.

“These become particularly key at midlife as women experience age- and menopause-related changes in body composition, bone, and cardiometabolic health,” Faubion added.

Sources indicate that ross agreed that physical activity is crucial for more than just mood and mental health improvement. She also noted that there are other types of exercise beyond ABIs and MBAs that can benefit people during menopause:.

“These types of activities help with weight loss or allow women to maintain a healthy weight. If you are not ready for aerobic exercises, stretching and simple exercises help with balance and stability,” Ross stated.

Faubion told Healthline that physical activity is an important part of healthy aging and should be encouraged during the menopause transition, but it should not be suggested that women can simply exercise their way out of significant depression or other bothersome menopause symptoms.

“Women experiencing persistent depression, anxiety, or symptoms that interfere with their quality of life should seek evaluation and discuss the full range of evidence-based treatment options with their healthcare clinician,” Faubion noted.

  • After introducing the Neira Concept at the 2026 Gaikindo Indonesia International Auto Show (GIIAS) in July, Hyundai is gearing up to open pre-orders on November 20.
  • The Neira is a pretty “significant” deal as Hyundai’s first locally produced seven-seat electric SUV in Indonesia.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hyundai revealed the production-ready Neira EV for the first time, a three-row, seven-seat electric SUV set to launch in Indonesia on November 20.

After introducing the Neira Concept at the 2026 Gaikindo Indonesia International Auto Show (GIIAS) in July, Hyundai is gearing up to open pre-orders on November 20.

The Neira is a pretty “significant” deal as Hyundai’s first locally produced seven-seat electric SUV in Indonesia.

Ahead of its official debut on Friday at GAIKINDO Auto Week (GAW) 2026, Hyundai offered a closer look at the upcoming Neira.

In a recent development, the electric SUV is essentially a Hyundai-badged version of the Kia Carens Clavis EV that introduced last year. Aside from the Hyundai logos, a few minor tweaks to the front and rear ends, and new wheels and headlights, it’s a near replica.

Inside, both are equipped with dual 12.3″ instrument display and center navigation screens, plus an added climate control panel.

Hyundai didn’t reveal battery or powertrain specs, but the Neira is expected to use the same 42 kWh and 51.4 kWh battery packs as the Carens Clavis EV. The former offers an MIDC range of up to 251 mi (404 km), while the latter has up to 304 mi (490 km) on a single charge.

Both batteries can be charged from 10% to 80% in around 39 minutes using a 100 kW DC fast charger.

The Kia Carens Clavis is 4,550 mm long, 1,800 mm wide, and 1,708 mm tall, with a 2,780 mm wheelbase, so Hyundai’s Neira will likely be about the same size, if not slightly bigger.

Hyundai said the Neira has four key advantages: A higher ground clearance, Hyundai Bluelink connectivity tech, a Blind-spot View Monitor (BVM), and easy third-row access.

A post shared by Hyundai Motors Indonesia (@hyundaimotorindonesia).

Ahead of its upcoming launch, Hyundai is taking the electric 7-seater on a trip to prove its capabilities, going from Kilometer Nol in Banda Aceh to Banda Neira, which is about 4,000 kilometers (about 2,500 miles).

While Hyundai may export the Neira EV to overseas markets like India, don’t expect it to reach the US.

Hyundai already sells a three-row, seven-seat electric SUV, the IONIQ 9, which is built at Hyundai’s Metaplant in Georgia.

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1317 w)
📖 Baca
General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Electrek ↗ Open Full Page

Iceland’s first wind farm comes with a water-saving bonus

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1317 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Iceland’s first utility-scale wind farm comes with a useful perk: When the wind picks up, its hydropower reservoirs can save water for later.
  • Vaðölduver Wind Farm plugs straight into the existing Búrfell hydropower infrastructure, sharing 220 kV transmission lines, substations, and access roads.
  • Industry observers note that landsvirkjun, Iceland’s national power company, officially commissioned Vaðölduver on September 15, 2026.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Iceland’s first utility-scale wind farm comes with a useful perk: When the wind picks up, its hydropower reservoirs can save water for later.

Vaðölduver Wind Farm plugs straight into the existing Búrfell hydropower infrastructure, sharing 220 kV transmission lines, substations, and access roads. And Iceland’s windiest months coincide with the time of year when less water flows into its reservoirs.

Industry observers note that landsvirkjun, Iceland’s national power company, officially commissioned Vaðölduver on September 15, 2026. The first 14 turbines are online; another 14 will be installed in a second phase, and the entire wind farm is expected to be operating by the end of 2027.

Industry observers note that once complete, Vaðölduver will have 120 megawatts (MW) of capacity. When I met with the folks at Landsvirkjun in Reykjavik last month, they told me that’s enough to power the equivalent of 90,000 Icelandic households. Vaðalda’s electricity feeds into the grid and is sold through power purchase agreements.

Vaðölduver sits on a lava-and-sand plain east of the Þjórsá River, south of Sultartangi Dam. Landsvirkjun already operates seven hydropower stations in the surrounding Þjórsá and Tungnaá region.

The wind farm was sited in this region of Iceland because the seasons line up nicely.

The winds are strongest in winter, when inflows into hydropower reservoirs can be low. In summer, wind speeds tend to drop, but glacial melt increases water availability for the hydropower system.

Recent findings suggest that when the wind turbines are generating plenty of electricity, Landsvirkjun can ease off hydropower and leave more water in its reservoirs. When the wind drops, hydropower can pick up more of the demand.

That gives the utility more control over when it uses its stored water and helps that water go further.

Sources indicate that german wind turbine maker Enercon manufactured Vaðölduver’s turbines. The project also includes a service and maintenance agreement with Enercon.

Sources indicate that landsvirkjun had a decade of experience operating pilot wind turbines before building Vaðölduver. One substantial thing they learned: They didn’t need tall towers to find plenty of wind.

In a recent development, there’s little vegetation or other surface obstructions across this unique, exposed landscape. That allows the turbines to capture productive winds closer to the ground than they could at a more wooded or sheltered location.

“Lower” is relative, of course. The turbines still reach 150 meters (492 feet) at their highest blade tip.

Recent findings suggest that the wind farm covers 17.1 square kilometers (6.6 square miles). Twenty-five turbines are rated at 4.26 MW each, and the remaining three at 4.5 MW. Landsvirkjun’s presentation puts annual generation at 440 GWh and lists a P50 net efficiency figure of 43%, which is considered strong for onshore wind.

Recent findings suggest that the ability to tap into existing infrastructure was a major factor in Landsvirkjun’s site selection. Where a wind farm goes affects its cost, its environmental footprint, and the people who live nearby.

According to recent reports, landsvirkjun also identifies active engagement with communities and other stakeholders as essential to building wind projects. At Vaðölduver, the immediate task is to finish the remaining 14 turbines while the first phase completes its trial runs.

It has been revealed that the tech giant sees wind as a potential third pillar of Iceland’s electricity supply alongside hydropower and geothermal. Vaðölduver highlights how those resources can work together, with wind adding generation while helping conserve stored water.

Sources indicate that iceland is a world leader in clean energy. It generates nearly 100% of its electricity from renewable sources, combining hydropower fueled by glacial runoff and rivers (around 70%) and geothermal energy (around 30%).

Over 90% of Icelandic households use direct geothermal hot water for space heating and hot water, while the remaining homes use renewable electricity.

But it’s got the same grid capacity challenges as every other country. Adding wind – and anything else that uses power – means paying close attention to what the grid can handle. Iceland has an isolated transmission system, so maintaining stability and ensuring sufficient capacity are increasingly vital as the country develops more projects.

While in Reykjavik, I met with the Minister of the Environment, Energy and Climate, Jóhann Páll Jóhannsson, who told me that the Icelandic grid’s capacity is expected to grow from 20 TWh to 24-25 TWh within a decade. Jóhannsson also said that he is pro-data center and that investors are keen to establish more of them in the country.

Industry observers note that when I asked Jóhannsson and his team, as well as the teams at Landsvirkjun and publicly owned ON Power, Iceland’s second-largest electricity generator and largest EV charger network, about grid expansion prepares to handle that pipeline, they all said that legislative reforms were being passed to speed up energy permitting processes. There is also financing in place to grow the grid. The physical transmission network is being expanded, but the process is slow because NIMBYism is creating bottlenecks.

In learning about latest and completed Icelandic power projects during my visit, it was apparent that the companies in the power and geothermal heat sector regularly collaborate on projects – everyone brings their expertise to the table and works for the common good (yes, really).

Sources indicate that but what was striking in discussions about grid expansion was that there seemed to be no plans to pitch in with the Icelandic transmission system operator (TSO), Landsnet hf. It seemed that the plan was to let the TSO come up with the solutions on its own. At most, Jóhannsson’s team stated its legislative reform “opened the door” to possible grid innovations.

When I asked the Landsvirkjun team whether they were considering working with the TSO on distributed energy resource (DER) projects like virtual power plants and onsite battery storage for its heavy-industry clients, which make up 80% of its business, they said they hadn’t considered it.

I often wonder why Quebec hasn't followed this strategy. They have huge dams with world-leading power connections, and one of the issue they are facing is a lack of water to refill those dams, due to several years of relative drought. I know it costs a lot to build wind power up north, but siting a project there would re-use their massive investment in power lines. The dams would act as gigantic batteries, because they wouldn't need to drain their reservoirs when the wind is blowing.

Industry observers note that iceland has earned its reputation as a clean energy leader. Bringing that same collaborative and creative approach to expanding its grid would help it keep setting an example for the rest of the world.

#98555. Ultra-Processed Food Intake May Increase Dementia, Stroke Risk

📅 18 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (841 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚠️ Warning 🌐 Healthline ↗ Open Full Page

Ultra-Processed Food Intake May Increase Dementia, Stroke Risk

📅 18 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (841 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Healthy adults who eat high levels of ultra-processed foods (UPFs) may be more likely to show signs of damage to the brain that could increase the likelihood of stroke and future memory problems, according to a study published October 15 in JAMA Network Open.
  • In a recent development, UPFs are often defined using the NOVA classification: These foods typically have 5 or more ingredients and include substances not typically found in culinary preparations.
  • UPFs account for more than 50% of daily energy intake in high-income countries, including the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Healthy adults who eat high levels of ultra-processed foods (UPFs) may be more likely to show signs of damage to the brain that could increase the likelihood of stroke and future memory problems, according to a study published October 15 in JAMA Network Open.

In a recent development, UPFs are often defined using the NOVA classification: These foods typically have 5 or more ingredients and include substances not typically found in culinary preparations. This category of foods includes packaged snack foods, sugary cereals, soft drinks, and frozen ready-to-eat meals.

UPFs account for more than 50% of daily energy intake in high-income countries, including the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom.

Previous research has linked these foods to adverse cardiometabolic outcomes. This newly introduced study adds to growing evidence linking high UPF intake to adverse health outcomes.

Recent findings suggest that this was a cross-sectional analysis of 8,783 adults between the ages of 35 and 69 without cardiovascular disease. The participants were all enrolled in the Canadian Alliance for Healthy Hearts and Minds (CAHHM) and Prospective Urban and Rural Epidemiology-MIND (PURE-MIND) cohorts.

In a recent development, the researchers used MRI scans to evaluate the participants’ brains. They also set out to analyze the cross-sectional relationship between UPF consumption, body fat, vascular brain injury (VBI), and cognitive performance.

In a recent development, they measured the participants’ habitual UPF intake using a food frequency questionnaire. Intake was expressed as servings based on a 2,000-calorie-per-day diet.

UPFs accounted for an average of 25% of participants’ daily diets. For the individuals with the highest intake, this increased to 45% of everything on their plates, compared to 16% for those who ate the least.

Sources indicate that the researchers also noted that UPFs were not just an added part of individual diets. These foods appeared to replace whole foods.

Recent findings suggest that among people with the highest UPF intake, fruits, vegetables, grains, and other minimally processed foods accounted for 41% of their daily food intake. Among those with the lowest UPF intake, minimally processed foods made up 68% of their daily intake.

When the researchers compared the highest intake to the lowest, they found that those with a higher intake of UPFs had 1.7% more body fat. They also found that people with a higher UPF intake had higher odds of VBI.

“These findings are concerning, but it is vital to remember that an association does not prove cause and effect,” mentioned Michelle Routhenstein, Preventive Cardiology Dietitian at Entirely Nourished, who wasn’t involved in the study.

“From my perspective as a preventive cardiology dietitian, these findings reinforce the importance of nourishing our blood vessels to support both cardiovascular and brain health.”.

Although researchers found no significant differences in cognitive performance, the signs of vascular brain injury observed in the study have been associated with an increased risk of stroke and cognitive decline.

These findings suggest a possible link between UPF intake and signs of brain changes. However, participants were only assessed once and weren’t followed over time. This means the researchers were unable to determine whether UPFs directly caused the changes.

“While we can’t conclude from this study that limiting UPFs would improve brain health, we have decades of literature demonstrating that higher intakes of green leafy vegetables, brightly colored fruits, whole grains, and lean protein sources are good for brain health,” noted Suzanne Judd, PhD, Director of the UC College of Medicine’s Center for Public Health, who wasn’t involved in the study.

“So focusing more on what can be brought into the diet rather than what should be eliminated might be a good way to start,” she added.

The preservatives [in UPFs] may have a direct impact on the vascular system, while the loss of antioxidants results in a less robust response to inflammation in the body.

“Additionally, sugar or salt is often added to make the food a bit tastier so people consume it in higher quantities. Over-consumption of food can lead to weight gain and diabetes, which can negatively impact brain health,” Judd mentioned.

Judd told Healthline that it is virtually impossible to completely avoid UPFs. Even some “health” foods, like protein powder and some yogurts, are considered ultra-processed.

It is more key to look at diet overall and emphasize consuming foods as close to their natural state as possible, such as fruits, vegetables, grains, and meats purchased raw or frozen and then cooked at home.

Routhenstein recommended starting simply with one manageable swap rather than trying to overhaul your entire diet.

Sources indicate that she mentioned that you should identify an ultra-processed food you eat regularly and consider a more nutrient-rich alternative. It is important to account for convenience, food preferences, budget, and lifestyle so that the change feels realistic and is sustainable over the long term.

“I want people to feel empowered, not fearful, when making food choices,” said Routhenstein. “Healthy eating does not mean having to cook everything from scratch. What matters most is building consistent, nourishing habits that support both heart and brain health.”.

Sources indicate that when it comes to mountain towns, there’s good, there’s great, and then there’s Aspen—so needless to say, Aspen’s hotels are the height of luxury. Among one of the world’s finest ski towns (with a whopping four mountains on one lift ticket), this winter wonderland is rife with dazzling accommodations. The best hotels in Aspen offer everything: luxury spa experiences; fine dining; ski-in, ski-out access; and all the après-ski cocktails you can get your hands on.

If resort life isn’t quite your speed, fear not—there are plenty of picture-perfect rentals you can snag on Airbnb or Vrbo. Expect a robust selection of spacious condominiums, luxury mountain chalets, and backcountry cabins, most of which are within walking distance from one of Snowmass or Aspen Mountain’s peak-reaching gondolas and ski resorts.

Industry observers note that don’t love the snow? Good thing Aspen is a top-tier year-round destination. Ideal for climbers, equestrians, cyclists, and other adventure-seekers, the Rocky Mountains provide a backdrop for just about any summertime alpine experience you can dream up. The town’s famed Food & Wine Classic in June is also a can’t miss. Each luxury hotel and off-the-beaten-path rental we found offers access to some of the best adventures in the West, whether you visit in January, July, or anytime in between. Consider this your cue to scroll below and book your stay while date availability lasts.

Perks: Daily champagne sabering, full-service spa, heated outdoor pool, multiple on-site restaurants, pet-friendly, valet parking.

For the ultimate choice in old-school luxury, check in to the St. Regis. The grand, chalet-style property sits at the foot of Aspen Mountain—just a five-minute walk from the Silver Queen Gondola—and pairs classic Rocky Mountain charm with five-star hospitality. Inside, rooms are outfitted with buttery leather headboards, fine linens, marble bathrooms, and mountain views framed by mahogany trim, while the hotel’s on-call butler service can handle tasks like unpacking luggage and drawing a post-ski bath. The RAKxa Wellness Spa remains one of the best in town, offering oxygen facials, a heated outdoor pool (perfect for a post-slopes soak), and many more wellness-minded amenities. Still, this grande dame doesn’t take itself too seriously. Since 2023, it’s been home to The Snow Lodge, a winter spinoff of Montauk’s famed Surf Lodge. The après scene here has become the hottest ticket in Aspen—Diplo, Rampa, and Bob Moses have all spun sets in the open-air courtyard—while the group’s fresh supper club and nightlife concept brings coastal-cool energy to the Rockies with candlelit dinners, Champagne towers, and late-night dancing under the stars. It’s a rare blend of heritage and hedonism—the kind of place where you can trade ski boots for stilettos without missing a beat. From $649 per night.

The only AAA Five Diamond–rated hotel in Aspen, the Little Nell blends the best of the West with the cosmopolitan luxuries you’d expect from a five-star hotel. Every detail is dialed in. Guests can unwind at the heated outdoor pool and hot tub, book a treatment at the Little Nell Spa, or rely on the property’s Les Clefs d’Or–certified concierge team, who have a reputation for making the impossible happen (heli-skiing trip to Telluride, anyone?). Food and wine take center stage here, too—the hotel’s Chefs & Somms dinners pair Michelin-caliber cuisine with rare vintages from a 20,000-bottle cellar, one of the most impressive in the Rockies. But it’s on the mountain where The Little Nell truly shines. The Ski Concierge team can arrange first tracks before the lifts open, snowcat powder tours, or private gear fittings in your room, ensuring you’re perfectly prepped with your helmet and bindings. From $800 per night.

Perks: Rooftop hot tub, lobby bar and restaurant, pet-friendly, EV charging.

Industry observers note that for a quieter boutique experience, you’ll want to stay at Mollie Aspen. Opened in late 2023, the hotel blends Japanese and Scandinavian design, creating an atmosphere that feels immediately restorative. Roomy plush leather chairs, well-worn rugs, custom woodwork, and a plethora of unique design accents welcome weary travelers and exhausted skiers, exuding the type of vibe you’d expect from a well-loved and hard-to-reach mountain chalet. Despite the tucked-away vibe, Mollie’s location couldn’t be more central—you’re steps from downtown’s galleries, the Aspen Art Museum, and cultural landmarks like the Aspen Institute and Wheeler Opera House. If you’re too tired for a jaunt downtown, the Mollie also has a lobby restaurant and poolside rooftop bar where you can while away the hours. The rooftop, in particular, has become a gathering spot for the design-savvy après crowd, offering mountain views and mellow vinyl playlists. From $278 per night.

Perks: All-suite accommodations, outdoor heated lap pool and hot tub, fitness center, tennis and pickleball courts, shuttle service.

Sources indicate that backed up against the Rocky Mountains, Aspen Meadows Resort is a midcentury masterpiece tailor-made for design aficionados. Originally conceived as part of the Aspen Institute campus by artist and architect Herbert Bayer, the property is steeped in Bauhaus principles, with clean lines, geometric forms, and a playful use of primary colors throughout its public and private spaces. Best for art and design nerds, the resort’s 98 suites feature Bauhaus-inspired furnishings, while common spaces include art exhibitions, outdoor sculptures, and West End Social, a recently redesigned restaurant with aspen-wood paneling, Colorado marble, and colorful textiles. Some of the stand-out amenities include a shuttle service with routes into town and the Aspen airport, a heated saline pool and hot tub, and ski butler service. When you’re looking to venture outside of the hotel’s chic walls, there are 40 acres to explore, which include plenty of great sledding hills for those visiting in the winter months and a massive sculpture collection. There’s also the on-site Resnick Center for Herbert Bayer Studies, where rotation exhibitions explore the artist’s legacy. With so much space for playing, there are more activities for visitors than could fit into 10 different trips. Can’t-miss itinerary items include themed scavenger hunts, hot-air balloon rides, fly fishing, snowshoeing, and—of course—lots of skiing. From $359 per night.

Perks: Airport shuttle, pet-friendly, on-site fitness room, rooftop lounge.

For travelers who want to be right in the heart of it all, The Limelight Hotel Aspen offers front-row access to the town’s best shops, restaurants, and bars—plus it’s just steps from the Silver Queen Gondola, which whisks skiers to the top of Aspen Mountain in under 20 minutes. The atmosphere is lively yet low-key, thanks to communal spaces like the buzzy lounge, where locals and visitors gather for wood-fired pizzas, live music, and craft cocktails. The property staff helps guests craft the perfect stay, with activities including hiking adventures, whitewater rafting, art museum visits, and more. Some rooms feature balconies and patios and are draped in mountain charm (think: wool blankets and fireplaces). From $299 per night.

Perks: Mountain view, wood-burning fireplace, fully equipped kitchen, in-unit laundry, hot tub, security system, free parking, housekeeping available for a fee.

Sources indicate that just a block from the Silver Queen Gondola, this newly renovated two-bedroom condo makes it easy to spend mornings skiing Aspen Mountain and afternoons exploring the restaurants, boutiques, and après-ski spots in Aspen’s downtown area. Inside, cozy furnishings and a wood-burning fireplace make the living room an inviting place to warm up after a day on the slopes. The two bedrooms offer flexible sleeping arrangements, with a king bed in the primary suite and two twins that can be converted into another king in the second bedroom. The kitchen is outfitted with stainless steel appliances, an induction cooktop, and all the cooking equipment needed to whip up dinner at home, though with Ajax Tavern so close, you might not bother. From $865 per night.

Perks: Heated outdoor pool, fully equipped kitchen, in-unit laundry, pet-friendly, free parking.

There is a lot of architectural woodwork to behold in this modern Aspen condo, but thanks to an abundance of windows, the effect reads bright and airy rather than moody ski lodge. Paneled ceilings, exposed timber rafters, wood floors, and floor-to-ceiling cabinetry bring plenty of warmth to the interiors, while clean-lined furnishings give the two-bedroom space a more contemporary feel. Equipped with one king bedroom and one queen, the condo is particularly well suited to two couples traveling together or a family of four. In the exteriors, the heated pool offers another way to unwind, though the slopes are hardly far away: The property sits just off the Lower Corkscrew run on Aspen Mountain, steps from Lift 1A. From $1,272 per night.

Perks: Mountain views, private patio, soaking tub, in-unit laundry, free parking, pet-friendly, housekeeping available for a fee.

Aspen's Victorian-era architecture is every bit as charming as its mountain scenery, and this one-bedroom apartment near Pioneer Park puts you in the middle of one of the town's most scenic historic neighborhoods. Recently remodeled, the 540-square-foot space has bright, sunlight interiors that includes an open-blueprint kitchen and living room that seems considerably larger thanks to oversized windows lining the walls. A queen bedroom separates guests from the main living area, and modern conveniences like air-conditioning, a dishwasher, and in-unit laundry make longer stays especially comfortable. Although the apartment sits on a peaceful residential street, downtown Aspen's restaurants, boutiques, and the historic Wheeler Opera House are just a short walk away, and a nearby bus stop makes getting to the ski slopes easy. From $391 per night.

Perks: Wrap-around deck, washer and dryer, wood burning fireplace, Wi-fi.

Sources indicate that tucked just behind the St. Regis, this one-bedroom apartment puts you right in the center of Aspen without feeling caught in the crowd. The interiors are warm and functional rather than flashy—a wood-burning fireplace, buttery cotton linens from Garnier-Thiebaut, and plenty of closet space for your suitcases give the space an easy, lived-in comfort. A wraparound deck nearly doubles the footprint, inviting morning coffee in the sun or an après-ski glass of wine with views of the surrounding peaks. Everything is set up to make a stay feel effortless. There’s dedicated parking, air conditioning, and in-unit laundry, plus a Sonos sound system and high-speed Wi-Fi for streaming or working remotely. The open kitchen has all the essentials, while the living room feels like a natural place to gather after a day outside. Professionally managed by Aspen Vacations, guests enjoy thoughtful extras—an invitation to the members-only Caribou Club, and insider tips on local dining and trail access are just a couple to name. Steps from world-class restaurants, boutiques, and the Silver Queen Gondola, this retreat feels equal parts modern pied-à-terre and alpine hideaway—a polished perch for soaking in the best of Aspen, no ski-valet required. From $408 per night.

Perks: Fireplace, free parking, washer and dryer, shared pool and hot tub.

Right on the edge of downtown Aspen, this riverfront condo feels worlds away from the bustle. Floor-to-ceiling windows frame the Roaring Fork River, filling the space with natural light and the sound of rushing water. Inside, the palette is crisp and minimal—soft grays, creamy whites, and natural wood—letting the view take center stage. The open living area flows onto a private balcony, and a sleek kitchen with stainless appliances and stone counters may convince you to eat in. Better yet, there’s some practical touches, like in-unit laundry and high-speed internet, as well as amenities more commonly seen in hotels, such as a shared indoor pool, hot tub, and gym. From $412 per night.

Industry observers note that A WHITE DRESS shirt earns its place in your closet because you can wear it to a wedding on Saturday and back to work on Monday. But fit is everything. Nothing beats going custom or getting fitted in person, but you don’t need to spend a fortune at a tailor to find one that looks good. We found shirts online for a wide range of builds, including options with separate neck and sleeve sizing that can get you closer to the right fit off the rack.

The Men’s Health style team wore these shirts through commutes and long days at the office. We looked for shirts that fit well without alterations and still felt comfortable hours later. Some have the crisp feel you want with a suit; others have enough stretch that you won’t be thinking about your shirt all day. Here are the nine that made the cut.

Charles Tyrwhitt gives you more ways to get the fit right without visiting a tailor. You can choose your neck and sleeve measurements, then pick from classic, slim, or extra slim cuts. Style editor Joseph Cheatham wore the classic fit and found it roomy through the chest and shoulders without looking baggy under a jacket.

Recent findings suggest that the cotton twill has a bit of heft, so it looks right at home in an office without feeling too heavy on a summer commute. It also lived up to its non-iron billing: After a 40-minute commute and a full day of meetings, Cheatham went straight to an event without needing to steam or press it. If you like the fit but want a lighter fabric, Charles Tyrwhitt also makes shirts in poplin. Once you’ve nailed your size, keep an eye out for the brand’s multi-buy deals before stocking up.

Sources indicate that this Van Heusen shirt makes a decent case for spending less. Our testers liked the relaxed fit through the shoulders and chest, and found that it kept its shape after multiple washes. The polyester-cotton poplin also resisted wrinkles during wear, so it’s an easy option to keep in rotation for work.

The fabric is thin, though, and a white undershirt can help keep it from looking see-through. The regular cut gives you plenty of room, but it won’t have the close fit or substantial feel of the pricier shirts on this list. A point collar and adjustable cuffs keep it looking presentable under a jacket.

Lululemon’s updated Venture looks like a dress shirt, but its lightweight polyester blend feels much better on a hot commute. Cheatham wore it under a blazer on a muggy subway ride, then kept it on through a full workday and dinner without overheating. The fabric wicks away sweat, and its stretch let him lift his arms without the shirt tugging at his shoulders.

In a recent development, it has a relaxed fit through the chest and waist, plus removable collar stays that keep it looking sharp under a jacket. You can also put it in the washer and dryer; we found it came out ready to wear without ironing. The trade-off is the feel. If you like a crisp cotton dress shirt, this one will feel more like performance wear. And unlike similarly priced shirts at Charles Tyrwhitt, you can’t customize the fit with separate neck and sleeve sizes.

Brooks Brothers’ stretchy dress shirt lets you breathe. No really, one of our editors, who has a significant chest, claims he can reach and sit comfortably in this without feeling like a button is going to pop off. That’s because it’s blended with plenty of spandex. Even better: it's made with Supima cotton, an extra-long staple cotton that’s softer, stronger, and more durable than regular cotton.

In a recent development, our tester put this through more than six washes over the last few months, and it hasn’t lost its pure white color. The non-iron cloth-like material doesn’t flinch at tons of movement, so we never spotted a wrinkle. Plus, the adjustable double-button cuffs at the wrist add a nice, polished touch.

It comes in three fits: Slim, which is the most tailored cut with a higher armhole that sits closer to the body; Traditional, the more relaxed style for maximum room; and Regular, the brand’s standard designed for a wide range of body types. I tried the traditional, which is forgiving in the stomach, especially if you’ve just inhaled a burger and fries.

Industry observers note that our testers with athletic builds found Suitsupply’s white shirt especially comfortable. The slim fit gave them a cleaner shape through the waist without pulling across the chest, which can be a problem when you have broader shoulders. The Egyptian cotton feels soft against the skin but still looks crisp under a blazer.

The shirt held its shape and color through multiple washes in our testing. It did pick up a few wrinkles during a rushed commute, so don’t count on it to stay perfectly pressed all day. Our testers liked how it looked without a jacket, too: the close cut gave it shape without leaving extra fabric billowing around the waist.

Sources indicate that banana Republic’s slim-fit option is top-tier because you get that bespoke look straight off the rack without the cost of custom tailoring. Cut closer to the body, it avoids the extra fabric bunching at the waist or billowing under a blazer. It looks especially sharp at cocktail receptions where you want a cleaner, crisp vibe. Plus, the cotton fabric lies flat across the chest, so you won’t see those distracting crease lines running down the middle.

Unlike others on the list, the brand offers tons of colors and patterns, in case you want to grab some alternatives to white. The spread collar is wider than most of the options we’ve tested, but it adds balance if you’ve got broader shoulders or a wider face, since it evens out proportions. I wore it through a hot, crowded commute and noticed the fabric stayed breathable without feeling stiff. Even after hours of typing and reaching for things on set, the shirt never tugged or felt restrictive.

In a recent development, on a hot, 80-degree day, I figured this white dress shirt would show sweat rings under my arms or across the chest and look sloppy before lunch. But I was wrong—it handled heat and crowding better than most plain cotton shirts I’ve worn. Even after back-to-back meetings and even post-work drinks, I still looked sharp. That’s because Calvin Klein combined a cotton-spandex blend with a non-iron finish, so the fabric feels cottony—not plasticky—and keeps shallow creases from setting, after hours of sitting and moving around.

In a recent development, the generous cut across the chest and shoulders kept it comfortable without ballooning at the sides. Plus, the stretch really came through when I hauled my bag into the subway rack, flagged down a cab, or leaned over my laptop. I found the point collar stayed neat all day, so I didn’t look sloppy after ditching my blazer. I even folded it into my bag for a short trip, and it bounced back with just a few light lines—nothing that called for an iron before heading out again.

Sources indicate that the Jack has taken more than 10 trips through the wash in our tester’s rotation, and it still hasn’t frayed or lost its color. That’s the case for calling it our most durable pick. The Oxford cotton is thicker and more textured than a typical dress shirt, but it feels soft rather than stiff.

Industry observers note that technically, this is a button-down, not a formal dress shirt. The close cut and higher armholes keep it from looking boxy, though, and our tester found it looked good tucked into trousers or left untucked for dinner. A rounded chest pocket gives it a little character. The collar buttons down, so the points stay put.

Sources indicate that there’s no stretch in the cotton, so consider sizing up if shirts tend to pull across your chest. It wrinkles a bit, too. Wear this one where the dress code gives you some room.

Billy Reid’s oxford white dress shirt is a step up from your typical oxford shirt. It has a finer texture, a button-down collar, and a center-back pleat, that keeps this shirt polished enough for a fancy dinner or a day at the country club. Speaking of which, the chest pocket is a smart touch for golfers who want to hang tight to their tees and scorecards. As a 5'8" guy with a slender build, I found the standard fit feels just right. It’s roomy across my shoulders and chest to swing a golf club or reach across a conference table, yet tailored enough at the waist to keep a clean, sharp silhouette.

The cotton fabric has enough heft to drape cleanly over the shoulders and chest without looking stiff. Even the stitching and button placement are tastefully done, so everything sits neatly on the body, giving off a more upscale, tailored vibe without being overly formal. It’s durable enough to handle regular wear like Taylor Stitch’s oxford shirt, but it wrinkles less. Sure, it can take a wash, but I stick to dry cleaning when I want it to look truly fresh.

Sources indicate that cotton is the gold standard for dress shirts, with Egyptian and Supima cotton being the softest and most durable. Cotton blends with a bit of stretch add comfort and flexibility for all-day wear.

Poplin (or broadcloth) is smooth and lightweight, giving a crisp, formal look.

Twill and Oxford weaves are slightly heavier, more textured, and naturally resist wrinkles.

Slim fit shirts offer a sharp, tailored look that’s cut closer to the body with higher armholes. They can feel snug if you have broad shoulders. Best for lean or trim guys.

The most versatile cut, with more room through the chest and waist while still looking clean. Works for most body types and is a safe everyday option.

In a recent development, trim at the waist but roomier up top. Best for guys with broad shoulders, bigger chests, or muscular builds who hate feeling boxed in.

According to recent reports, spread collars are versatile and look sharp with a tie but also sleek open. The points angle out wider, leaving more room between them. Best for broader faces or shoulders since it balances proportions.

In a recent development, the most classic style, with collar tips that point down closer together. Works on pretty much everyone, helps elongate the face, and is the most versatile for office-to-event dressing.

According to recent reports, the tips fasten with buttons to the shirt. More casual and relaxed, perfect for business-casual offices or weekends out. Also works well under sweaters or open without a tie.

It has been revealed that we first published this story in 2019, and we’ve revisited the picks as we’ve tested upcoming shirts. For this revision, I worked with Men’s Health style editor Joseph Cheatham and other members of our fashion team. We wore the shirts on commutes and through full days at work, paying attention to how they fit once we started moving around. A shirt can look great in the mirror and still pull across your chest the moment you sit down.

We also checked how the collars held up during wear and what happened after washing. For the white shirts, we looked for fabric that stayed bright and offered enough coverage. The picks earned their spots for different reasons: Charles Tyrwhitt gives you more ways to dial in the fit, while Lululemon’s lightweight shirt was the one we wanted on a hot commute.

For formal events or business settings, pairing a white dress shirt with a dark suit is a classic choice that never fails—the crispness of the white dress shirt against the darker suit creates a nice contrast that exudes professionalism—and you should complement it with a tie and polished leather dress shoes.

According to recent reports, for less formal dress codes in business-casual settings or smart-casual environments, wear white dress shirts with chinos or similar styles to look sharp but also smart. You can also roll up the sleeves slightly or leave the top buttons undone to look more relaxed. Here, you can match these shirts with loafers or even dress sneakers to look modern while feeling as comfortable as ever.

Industry observers note that to dress down with white dress shirts for casual outings or weekend gatherings, layer them under a well-fitted blazer or denim jacket to strike a balance between formal and relaxed. You can also wear these shirts untucked with jeans and khakis for a laid-back yet put-together appearance.
